s1.syndrome_frame: a cutaneous vascular lesion with telangiectasias on the lower extremity in a patient with a history of rectal adenocarcinoma and metastases
salient_findings: a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque on the lower right lateral shin
discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels on histopathological analysis
somatic KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R mutation identified on genetic analysis
key_facts: male patient in his 40s
weight: 109kg
diagnosed with stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma in November 2013
pulmonary and liver metastases present
treatment history includes radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
lesion developed on the lower right lateral shin in early January 2015
lesion is a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque
lesion is densely composed of telangiectasias
lesion measures 4 cm in diameter
lesion is not associated with pain or pruritus
histopathological analysis shows discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels
epidermis is normal on histopathological analysis
somatic KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R mutation identified on genetic analysis

differentials: hemangioma of the superficial lymphatic vessels
per_call: hemangioma of the superficial lymphatic vessels

shortlist.label: acquired tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: matches the clinical presentation of a cutaneous vascular lesion with telangiectasias and the presence of a somatic KDR (VEGFR2) mutation

shortlist.label: pyogenic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the histopathological findings of discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels and the clinical presentation of a blanchable red plaque

shortlist.label: microvenular hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the histopathological findings and the clinical presentation of a cutaneous vascular lesion

shortlist.label: bacillary angiomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: considered in the differential diagnosis due to the presence of a cutaneous vascular lesion, although less likely given the lack of systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: cutaneous metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: considered in the differential diagnosis due to the patient's history of rectal adenocarcinoma and metastases, although less likely given the clinical presentation and histopathological findings

raw.rationale: The presence of a somatic KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R mutation and the histopathological findings of discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels are consistent with acquired tufted angioma, which is a rare vascular lesion that can be associated with somatic mutations in the KDR gene.

rejected.label: pyogenic granuloma
rejected.why: While pyogenic granuloma can present as a bright red plaque, the histopathological findings and genetic analysis in this case are more consistent with acquired tufted angioma.

rejected.label: microvenular hemangioma
rejected.why: Microvenular hemangioma typically presents with a more complex vascular pattern and is not typically associated with somatic KDR mutations.

rejected.label: bacillary angiomatosis
rejected.why: Bacillary angiomatosis is typically associated with Bartonella infection and does not match the histopathological and genetic findings in this case.

rejected.label: cutaneous metastasis
rejected.why: Cutaneous metastasis would not typically present with the vascular pattern and genetic findings seen in this case, and would more likely be associated with the patient's underlying cancer.
